reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm survives the evidence test. The strongest apparent family, P-AC / P-DR / ... / P-CV, shares a prefix P-, but the residues do not contribute their standalone meanings compositionally inside the procedures: AC means a fault state ('chaotic flicker...'), while P-AC means a repair procedure, not 'P + chaotic flicker...'. This is best treated as an opaque procedure label series, not morphology. The T1–T14 series likewise fails the opaque index test: the digits do not contribute literal count meaning, but select distinct stored procedures. Orthographic similarities such as corner/corners, edge/edges, brief/bright, all/alt, and center/corner do not provide a reliable compositional paradigm with stable shared morpheme meanings across multiple entries. Because false morphology is worse than a flat lexicon, all supplied symbols are treated as lexical.
